provider.name: Cloudflare Workers with SQLite-backed Durable Objects

profiles.notes: Checked 2026-11-09 on the Workers and Durable Objects limits and pricing pages. Workers Free: 100,000 requests per day, 10 ms CPU per request, 128 MB memory, 50 subrequests per request. Durable Objects on Free: SQLite-backed only, 100,000 requests and 13,000 GB-s per day, 5 GB total storage, 5 million rows read and 100,000 rows written per day. The pages disagree on the per-object storage cap on Free (1 GB or 10 GB); not resolved here. A WebSocket connection costs one request and incoming messages count 1 in 20 for billing; whether the free daily limit uses the same ratio is not stated, so requestsPerDay may be wrong for live connections. No concurrent-connection limit is published, so concurrentPeople is omitted. A jurisdiction restricts where objects run; it is not a compliance certification, so compliance is empty.

provider.name: Cloudflare Workers with SQLite-backed Durable Objects

profiles.notes: Checked 2026-11-09 (same pages as cloudflare-free). Workers Paid: no request limit, CPU per request 30 seconds by default and up to 5 minutes, unlimited storage per account and 10 GB per Durable Object. Prices from the Workers and Durable Objects pricing pages: $5 per month minimum; Workers 10 million requests and 30 million CPU milliseconds included, then $0.30 per million requests and $0.02 per million CPU milliseconds; Durable Objects 1 million requests and 400,000 GB-s included, then $0.15 per million requests and $12.50 per million GB-s; SQLite storage 5 GB-month included then $0.20 per GB-month; rows written 50 million included then $1.00 per million. Duration is charged while an object is active or cannot hibernate, so hibernating WebSockets matter for cost. Prices and limits change; check the pages again before quoting them. Jurisdictions restrict where objects run and store data; this is not a compliance certification.

provider.name: Node http server on the owner's machine

profiles.notes: No provider limits apply and none were measured: limitsSource is null. The Node adapter runs one process on one machine, holds every live object in memory, rewrites an object's whole file on each change, and has no failover, so capacity depends on the machine and is not stated here. Hardware, electricity, a stable address, TLS termination and backups are the owner's cost and are not priced here. Region is wherever the machine is.

notes: Limits and prices for the two Cloudflare profiles come only from developers.cloudflare.com pages fetched on 2026-11-09: workers/platform/limits, workers/platform/pricing, durable-objects/platform/limits, durable-objects/platform/pricing, durable-objects/reference/data-location. The own-hardware profile cites no source.
